correctness.rationale: The susceptible equation integrates to the exponential final-size relation. The second fixed-point map is rational because the Laplace transform of the common exponential infectious lifetime is rational; the type-specific positive incubation rates do not affect the limiting fixed points in the absence of competing exposed-stage removal. Equal population sizes and balanced contacts give the stated transpose relation. Both row sums of the final-size matrix exceed one under the given assumptions, hence both matrices are supercritical. The standard Perron subsolution and the unit supersolution give existence; maximal coordinate ratio and strict subhomogeneity give uniqueness. There is also a direct check of the decisive two-dimensional rank lemma: for either response f, H(x)=f⁻¹(x)/x strictly increases. If x₁>x₂ for x=f(Mx), then H(x₁) is strictly below row sum 1 and H(x₂) is strictly above row sum 2, so row sum 1 exceeds row sum 2. Reverse the indices for the other inequality; equal coordinates force equal row sums. After removing the common positive factor the two calculated contrasts have the form α−ηβ and ηα−β for positive α,β. Their zeros are reciprocal: exactly one lies in [0,1) when α≠β, with one tie there, and neither lies there when α=β. For the vanishing deterministic seed, the final-size equation with a positive seed gives a nonzero supersolution of the unseeded map; it cannot approach zero, since multiplication by a positive left Perron vector contradicts supercriticality for a sufficiently small positive supersolution. The positive branch therefore has the asserted interpretation. The supporting verifier was read, not run; the exact argument is independent of samples.
